cycle_1_slots.instruction: Decide and record the DbWriter unbounded-channel question (OD-1).
cycle_1_slots.status: COMPLETE — DECIDED: keep the channel unbounded, and disclose a pathological backlog. Bounding it would force try_send (drops events, breaking the flush() contract) or an async submit() at a sync engine call site. The queue is also already bounded in practice by DEFAULT_MAX_ENTITIES=2500 and the wall-time watchdog. The real defect was that a storage stall was INVISIBLE, so writer_loop now discloses queue depth past BACKLOG_WARN_EVENTS=1024 with hysteresis at half.

observations.summary: A live scan is NOT a valid instrument for measuring entity-count differences here. Three runs at an IDENTICAL floor (0.30, same seed, depth 0) returned 543, 582 and 561 entities — a 39-entity spread driven by which search engines and modules happen to succeed. An apparent non-monotonicity (0.0 yielding 462 vs 0.30 yielding 543) is within that order of magnitude and is NOT evidence of a filter bug; the filter is monotonic by construction over a fixed entity set. Any future claim about relative entity counts needs a deterministic fixture, not a live scan.

track_cycle_4_slots.instruction: Establish why the dossier/debug bundle prints six zero module counters mid-scan, then fix it without fabricating numbers.
track_cycle_4_slots.outcome: DONE (d4238fa9b). Cause traced end to end: Scan::new seeds modules_* to 0; run_with_ledger_inner (core/engine/mod.rs:653) upserts the Running row with those zeros; the ONLY write is finalise_scan (core/engine/mod.rs:991-996) at scan end; nothing updates the row in between. observations_not_on_main_spine.observation: CLOSES OB-6. The mid-scan six-zero module counters are fully explained and fixed in cycle 4 slot 1. Evidence chain: Scan::new seeds zeros (core/scan/mod.rs) -> run_with_ledger_inner upserts Running with them (core/engine/mod.rs:653-654) -> finalise_scan is the sole writer (core/engine/mod.rs:991-996). Both uploaded debug bundles were status:Running, which is why both showed zeros while their event streams held ~70 module_start / ~60 module_done / ~9 module_error / ~11 module_skipped.

Deliberate design limit recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the event stream CANNOT reconstruct the engine's six counters. There is no distinct EventKind for a timeout (it arrives as a plain ModuleError), a cache replay, or a dedup; and ModuleSkipped is not disjoint from ModuleStart — gate-skips are emitted with no preceding start (Engine::emit_module_skipped, core/engine/mod.rs:477-482) while dispatched-then-opted-out modules emit one first (dispatch.rs:548). ModuleEventTally therefore reports event counts under their event names and offers no in-flight figure.
